sections.name: AIAssistantDrawer (part 1)
sections.title: Opening the panel and starting state
sections.what: Holds the typed text and chat history, starts with a welcome message, and listens for the Ctrl or Cmd, Shift and A shortcut to open or close the panel. The panel draws nothing when closed.
sections.why: Gives keyboard access and keeps the screen clean when hidden.

sections.name: AIAssistantDrawer (part 2)
sections.title: Sending a message and confirming a task
sections.what: On send, adds the owner's message, then either drafts a task from a reminder-like request or answers a question. If the AI call fails, it shows a notice. Confirming a draft adds a task with defaults such as 45 minutes and a todo status.
sections.why: Separates the two kinds of request and makes the owner approve tasks before they are saved.
sections.watch_out: The fallback notice describes a local engine that this code does not actually run.

sections.name: AIAssistantDrawer (part 3)
sections.title: Chat bubbles and task preview
sections.what: Shows the header, then the chat history with icons that differ for the owner and the assistant, plus a preview card for each drafted task showing date, time, priority and energy.
sections.why: Lets the owner read the conversation and check the parsed task before confirming.

sections.name: AIAssistantDrawer (part 4)
sections.title: Confirm button and input box
sections.what: Shows a confirm button on each task preview and an input box where pressing Enter or the send button submits the message.
sections.why: Gives the owner the controls to finish the exchange.

summary: A side panel chat where the owner types a request. It either drafts a task from a reminder-like sentence for confirmation, or answers a question about tasks, assignments, hackathons and habits.
purpose: Lets the owner create tasks in plain language and ask about their work.
why: Makes task entry faster than filling out a form.
how: The panel only appears when the assistant is open. It can be toggled with Ctrl or Cmd, Shift and A. When the owner sends a message, the code checks for words such as remind, create or task to decide between drafting a task and answering a question. Results appear as chat bubbles. A drafted task shows a preview with a confirm button that adds it to the store.
inputs: The owner's typed messages, the open state from the store, and the tasks, assignments, hackathons and habits from the store.
outputs: Chat bubbles, a task preview with a confirm button, and new tasks added to the store after confirmation.
risks: The owner's messages and their work data are sent to an outside AI provider when the assistant answers, so private details leave the app. If the AI call fails, the notice says it switched to a local engine, but no local engine is called in this file. The fallback flag is set but never shown. Message ids use the current time, so two messages in the same moment could clash.
debug: If replies never arrive, check the AI provider configuration and the browser console. If a task is wrong, check the parsed draft fields before confirming. If the panel does not open, check the keyboard shortcut handler and the open state in the store.
